From a Texas biplane ride to the Hall of Fame. ✈️

At 105, Nell “Mickey” Stevenson Bright is part of the International Air & Space Hall of Fame class honored November 21 at the San Diego Air & Space Museum.

Bright grew up in Canyon, Texas, where a childhood ride in a World War I biplane got her hooked on flying. In 1943 she joined the Women Airforce Service Pilots, becoming one of 1,074 women to earn WASP wings. She was among the first 20 women selected to train on the B-25 Mitchell and also flew the P-47.

A childhood ride lit the spark. A lifetime later, her story is still getting people excited about flying. Congratulations, Mickey.

Sources: Commemorative Air Force, November 25, 2026, and the San Diego Air & Space Museum.
